name: clear_cache
note: test-support: undocumented (\"Undocumented; some tests want it\", Lib/urllib/parse.py:95); clears the lru caches of urlsplit and _byte_quoter_factory, whose results do not depend on them

name: _encode_result
note: review: Its only entry, BytesTwin, runs it only on urlsplit's result object (mkRes through resEncode); its other use, encoding the str that urlunsplit/urlunparse build for bytes components (coerceStr true, :654/:681), is in no theorem, so a version returning that str unencoded passes.

name: _coerce_args
note: review: Its only entry, SplitRoundTrip, calls it with a str and None, so the 'Cannot mix str and non-str arguments' TypeError and the bytes/decode branch are never exercised; a version without the mixing check passes.

name: _NetlocResultMixinBase.port
note: review: PortSpec only fixes host:digits netlocs without '@', '[' or ':' in the host and netlocs without ':'; for 'h:abc', 'h:' or a bracketed or userinfo netloc only 'errors are ValueError' applies, so a port returning None for a non-digit port (CPython raises 'Port could not be cast') passes.

name: _SplitResultBase.geturl
note: review: Its entries only rebuild results of missing_as_none=True (_keep_empty true), so geturl on a default missing_as_none=False result is unpinned: a geturl calling urlunsplit(self, keep_empty=True), which raises there, passes.

name: _ParseResultBase.geturl
note: review: ParseRoundTrip only rebuilds missing_as_none=True results, so geturl on a default result is unpinned: one passing keep_empty=True (raising ValueError there) passes.

name: parse_qsl
signature: parse_qsl(qs, keep_blank_values=False, strict_parsing=False, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace', max_num_fields=None, separator='&', *, _stacklevel=1)
note: review: QslRoundTrip only uses keep_blank_values=True and defaults otherwise, so the separator check, strict_parsing errors, max_num_fields, blank dropping and None input are never exercised.

name: unquote_plus
note: review: Only QuotePlusRoundTrip names it, and it only unquotes quote_plus output (ASCII, valid escapes, decodable), so the errors argument, non-ASCII input and the bytes/None failures never run; a version ignoring errors passes.
